title: Insulin pen teaching before noon
objective: Plan teaching across cognitive, affective and psychomotor domains, and assess readiness to learn first
secondaryObjectives: Diagnosing, planning and evaluating with the person, not for them

brief.situation: 10:00 on a medical unit. You are the RN for Mr. Kim, 58, admitted with cellulitis of the foot and newly diagnosed type 2 diabetes. He starts a once-daily insulin pen at home. Discharge is set for 12:00, and the charge nurse asks you to 'get the teaching done'.
handover: His wife will help with his care at home; she arrives at 13:00 after work.
He has had no insulin teaching yet. His reading glasses are at home.

Unit policy: discharge teaching for a new injectable is complete only with a correct return demonstration and teach-back; the nurse tells the provider and case manager when discharge must move to finish it.
howItWorks: The clock runs in simulated time; study pace runs three simulated minutes per real minute. Pause any time.
Each check takes the time on its button. Decide what the findings mean, what to stop or start, and who must know.
Partway through you are asked to write your reasoning. A debrief scores what you did.

why.question: Is Mr. Kim ready to learn his insulin pen, and how will you teach it?

parts.label: What and why
parts.criteria: He is not ready yet: pain, no sleep, fear of needles and missing glasses block learning; he has misconceptions (cognitive), fear (affective) and a new skill to learn (psychomotor).
parts.modelAnswer: Not yet. He's hurting, exhausted, scared of needles and can't read the print. He's got wrong ideas about insulin, he's afraid, and he needs to learn a hands-on skill.

parts.label: What I do
parts.criteria: Treats pain first, plans with him across the three domains with large print, teaches by demonstration with his wife present, confirms with return demonstration and teach-back, and moves discharge with the provider and case manager.
parts.modelAnswer: Treat his pain, plan it with him: facts, his fears, then pen practice in big print. Have him and his wife both do it back to me and teach back the low-sugar signs, and get discharge moved.

noProgress.rationale: An unprepared discharge on a new injectable an hour on is harm here.

scoring.modelReasoning: Teaching starts with a learner assessment: is the client ready (tired, in pain, anxious), what do they already know, and what motivates them. Outcomes are planned in three domains: cognitive (knowledge: what insulin does, low-sugar signs), affective (feelings: his fear of needles and amputation) and psychomotor (the pen steps). A skill is evaluated by return demonstration and knowledge by teach-back. Mr. Kim is not ready at 10:00, so treat his pain, plan with him, involve his wife, confirm by return demonstration and teach-back, and move discharge rather than rush it.
